Convert an AnnData (h5ad) file to a Cerebro file

Source: R/convertH5adToCerebro.R
convertH5adToCerebro.Rd

One-step route from a .h5ad file, the container of the Python scverse ecosystem (AnnData, scanpy), to a .crb file that createShinyApp can serve. The file is read natively from HDF5 with readH5adAsSCE, so neither Python nor zellkonverter is needed, and the resulting SingleCellExperiment goes through convertSCEToCerebro, so every option of that route applies here too.

Usage

convertH5adToCerebro(
  h5ad_file,
  result_dir,
  assay = "X",
  use_raw = FALSE,
  modality = NULL,
  gene_names = NULL,
  airr = "auto",
  airr_sample = NULL,
  extra_modalities = NULL,
  experiment_name = NULL,
  organism = "Human",
  groups = NULL,
  groups_naming = NULL,
  max_group_levels = 100,
  nUMI = NULL,
  nGene = NULL,
  add_all_meta_data = TRUE,
  use_delayed_array = FALSE,
  expression_matrix_mode = c("embedded", "h5"),
  codec = c("qs2", "rds"),
  viewer_binary = c("auto", "always", "never"),
  viewer_binary_threshold = 100000L,
  verbose = TRUE,
  cell_cycle = NULL,
  main_group = NULL,
  projections = NULL,
  marker_file = NULL,
  marker_method = "Diff. Expression",
  add_most_expressed_genes = TRUE,
  most_expressed_genes = NULL,
  spatial_split_by = NULL,
  spatial_images = "auto"
)

Arguments

h5ad_file

Path to a .h5ad file (any anndata version, including the pre-0.7 layout), or to a MuData .h5mu file together with modality.

result_dir

Directory the .crb is written to (created if missing). The file is named cerebro_<basename>.crb.

assay

Which matrix to export: "X" (default) or the name of an entry of layers, e.g. "counts". With use_raw = TRUE the matrix is raw/X and this must stay "X".

use_raw

Use raw/X (and raw/var) as the expression matrix; see readH5adAsSCE.

modality

For a MuData file, the modality to convert (e.g. "gex"); see readH5adAsSCE.

gene_names

var column to use as gene names (default: the index, or a symbol column when the index is Ensembl IDs); see readH5adAsSCE.

airr

Immune receptor (TCR/BCR) data to import: "auto" (default) uses the MuData modality named airr, or obsm["airr"] of a plain h5ad, if the file has one, and imports nothing otherwise. Give a name to use another modality (or obsm entry), or FALSE to skip receptor data. See readH5adAsSCE.

airr_sample

obs column naming the sample of each cell, which keys the immune repertoire. By default orig.ident, sample, Sample or sample_id is used if present, else one sample.

extra_modalities

For an .h5mu file, other modalities to add to the expression data as extra features, for example "prot". Their features are named <modality>:<feature>. See convertSCEToCerebro, argument extra_features.

experiment_name, organism, groups_naming, max_group_levels, add_all_meta_data, use_delayed_array, expression_matrix_mode, codec, viewer_binary, viewer_binary_threshold, verbose, cell_cycle, main_group, projections, add_most_expressed_genes, most_expressed_genes

As in convertSCEToCerebro. experiment_name defaults to the file's base name.

groups

Character vector of obs columns to use as grouping variables. Required; an error lists the usable columns when omitted.

nUMI, nGene

obs columns holding transcripts and expressed genes per cell. By default the usual scanpy/Seurat names are looked for (total_counts, n_counts, nCount_RNA, nUMI and n_genes_by_counts, n_genes, nFeature_RNA, nGene); when none exists the values are computed from the counts layer (or from assay).

marker_file, marker_method

Optional marker table, as in convertSCEToCerebro. When given, it replaces the marker results taken from scanpy.

spatial_split_by

obs column dividing obsm["spatial"] into one section per level (e.g. the tissue sections of a MERFISH data set); see exportFromSCE.

spatial_images

Which Visium tissue images to embed ("auto", a vector of labels, or FALSE); see readH5adAsSCE.

Value

The path of the written .crb, invisibly.

Details

Category colours (uns["<column>_colors"]) are kept as the groups' default colours in the Viewer. Visium tissue images are embedded and drawn behind the spots; when a file has the images of several libraries (obs["library_id"]) each library becomes one section with its own image. The Viewer's Spatial plot has the y axis pointing up, so a Visium image, stored with row 0 on top, needs the vertical flip to line up with the spots: build the app with createShinyApp(..., spatial_image_settings = list(<dataset label> = list(spatial = list(hires = list(flip_y = TRUE))))). As for Seurat Visium objects, the coordinates are the file's, so the whole picture is then the mirror image (top to bottom) of the slide as drawn by scanpy.

scanpy's rank_genes_groups results, if present, are exported as marker genes. Embeddings in obsm (X_umap, X_tsne, X_pca, ...) become the projections; PCA is dropped when a non-PCA embedding exists, as on the other routes. Receptor chains written by scirpy (obsm["airr"]) fill the Immune repertoire page.

See also

readH5adAsSCE, convertSCEToCerebro

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
convertH5adToCerebro(
  h5ad_file = "pbmc.h5ad",
  result_dir = "output",
  groups = c("cell_type", "sample"),
  expression_matrix_mode = "h5"
)
} # }
